'''Jonathan Paul Clayden''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|CChem|FRSC}} (born 6 February 1968) is a Professor of [[organic chemistry]] at the [[University of Bristol]].

==Education and career==
Whilst at secondary school, he represented the UK at the [[International Chemistry Olympiad]] in 1986, winning a bronze medal. In 1992 he obtained his [[PhD]]<ref name="claydenphd">{{cite thesis |degree = PhD|first = Jonathan|last = Clayden|title = The asymmetric epoxidation of allylic phosphine oxides: a stereocontrolled synthesis of allylic systems|publisher = University of Cambridge|date = 1993|url = http://ulmss-newton.lib.cam.ac.uk/vwebv/holdingsInfo?bibId=16607|author-link = Jonathan Clayden}}</ref> at the [[University of Cambridge]] working with [[Stuart Warren|Dr Stuart Warren]] on [[asymmetric synthesis]] using [[phosphine oxide]] chemistry. He then carried out a postdoc with [[Marc Julia|Prof Marc Julia]] and in 1994 became a lecturer in [[organic chemistry]] at the [[University of Manchester]] where he became a reader in 2000 and a Professor of Organic Chemistry in 2001. In 2015 he moved to a chair in chemistry at the [[University of Bristol]]. He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2025/05/new-fellows/ |access-date=2025-05-22 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>

==Research==
His research interests encompass various areas of synthesis and stereochemistry, particularly where conformation has a role to play: asymmetric synthesis, atropisomerism,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Clayden|first1 = Jonathan|last2 = Moran|first2 = Wesley J.|last3 = Edwards|first3 = Paul J.|last4 = LaPlante|first4 = Steven R.|date = 2009-08-17|title = The Challenge of Atropisomerism in Drug Discovery|journal = Angewandte Chemie International Edition|language = en|volume = 48|issue = 35|pages = 6398–6401|doi = 10.1002/anie.200901719|issn = 1521-3773|pmid=19637174}}</ref> organolithium chemistry, remote stereochemical effects<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Byrne|first1 = Liam|last2 = Solà|first2 = Jordi|last3 = Boddaert|first3 = Thomas|last4 = Marcelli|first4 = Tommaso|last5 = Adams|first5 = Ralph W.|last6 = Morris|first6 = Gareth A.|last7 = Clayden|first7 = Jonathan|date = 2014-01-03|title = Foldamer-Mediated Remote Stereocontrol: >1,60 Asymmetric Induction|journal = Angewandte Chemie International Edition|language = en|volume = 53|issue = 1|pages = 151–155|doi = 10.1002/anie.201308264|issn = 1521-3773|pmid=24375739| url=https://pure.manchester.ac.uk/ws/files/29646381/POST-PEER-REVIEW-PUBLISHERS.PDF }}</ref> and dynamic foldamer chemistry.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Le Bailly|first1 = Bryden A. F.|last2 = Clayden|first2 = Jonathan|title = Dynamic foldamer chemistry|journal = Chem. Commun.|language = en|doi = 10.1039/c6cc00788k|pmid = 26955864|volume=52|issue = 27|pages=4852–4863|date = 2016-03-24|doi-access = free|hdl = 1983/8e0ce263-cb79-455f-b99e-40f2db2b8ba5|hdl-access = free}}</ref> He is one of the authors of the organic chemistry textbook - ''Organic Chemistry'' by Clayden, Greeves, Warren and Wothers.<ref>{{Cite book|title = Organic Chemistry|last1 = Clayden|first1 = Jonathan|last2 = Greeves|first2 = Nick|last3 = Warren|first3 = Stuart|publisher = OUP|year = 2012|isbn = 978-0-19-927029-3|location = Oxford|edition = Second}}</ref> He also wrote ''Organolithiums: Selectivity for Synthesis'',<ref>{{Cite book|title = Organolithiums: Selectivity for Synthesis|last = Clayden|first = Jonathan|publisher = Pergamon|year = 2002|isbn = 978-0-08-043261-8|location = Oxford}}</ref> which concerns the use of [[Organolithium reagent|organolithium compounds]] in organic synthetic reactions.

From 2005 to 2011 he was editor-in-chief of the Open Access [[Beilstein Journal of Organic Chemistry]].
